note: How to send leads from a tool to a job's lead address. {ADDRESS} stands for the address shown once when it was made. Consent: a lead arrives 'ask first' unless the tool also sends consent_text and consent_at.

guides.name: Zoho CRM
steps: In Zoho CRM open Setup, then Automation, then Workflow Rules (or Webhooks).
Make a rule on the Leads module: when a lead is created, run the action Webhook.
Set the webhook URL to {ADDRESS} and the method to POST, with the body type JSON (or form data).
Choose these fields in the body: Full Name as name, Mobile as phone, Email as email, City as city, Description as message and the Lead Id as external_id.
Save, then press Send a test lead here to see how a sample is understood.

guides.name: LeadSquared
steps: In LeadSquared open Settings, then API and Webhooks, then Webhooks.
Add a webhook for the event Lead creation (and Lead update if you want changes).
Set the URL to {ADDRESS}, method POST, content type JSON.
Map: FirstName to name, Phone (or Mobile) to phone, EmailAddress to email, mx_City to city, Notes to message and ProspectID to external_id.
Test it with a sample lead.

guides.name: Sell.Do
steps: In Sell.Do open Settings, then Integrations, then Webhooks.
Add a webhook on the event Lead created.
Set the URL to {ADDRESS} with method POST and format JSON.
Use these names: name, mobile (as phone), email, city, requirement (as message) and lead_id.
Press Send a test lead here to confirm.

guides.name: HubSpot
steps: In HubSpot open Automation, then Workflows, and make a contact-based workflow that starts when a contact is created.
Add the action Send a webhook.
Method POST, URL {ADDRESS}, authentication none (the address is the key).
In the request body choose: firstname as name, phone as phone, email as email, city as city, message as message and hs_object_id as external_id.
Turn the workflow on only after a test lead looks right.

guides.name: Zapier
steps: Make a Zap with your form or sheet as the trigger.
Add the action Webhooks by Zapier, then POST.
URL {ADDRESS}, payload type JSON.
Add the data fields: name, phone, email, city, message.
Test the step in Zapier, then press Send a test lead here to compare.

guides.name: Make (Integromat)
steps: Make a scenario with your form or sheet as the first module.
Add the module HTTP, then Make a request.
URL {ADDRESS}, method POST, body type JSON (application/json), input method JSON string.
Body: the fields name, phone, email, city and message from the first module.
Run the scenario once, then check the activity list here.

guides.name: n8n
steps: In your workflow add the node HTTP Request after your trigger.
Method POST, URL {ADDRESS}, Send Body on, body content type JSON.
Add the fields name, phone, email, city, message (use expressions from the trigger).
Execute the node, then look at the activity list here.

guides.name: Pabbly Connect
steps: Make a workflow with your form or sheet as the trigger.
Add the action API by Pabbly, then POST.
URL {ADDRESS}, payload type JSON.
Map name, phone, email, city and message.
Test the workflow and check the activity list here.

guides.name: Google Forms (Apps Script)
steps: Open your Google Form, then the three dots, then Script editor.
Paste the script below, replace the question titles if yours differ, and save.
In the script editor choose Triggers, add a trigger: function onSubmit, event source From form, event type On form submit.
Submit the form once yourself and look at the activity list here.
guides.note: Name your questions Name, Phone, Email, City and Message so they are understood.

guides.name: WordPress (a form plugin)
steps: Use any form plugin that can send a webhook (Contact Form 7 with a webhook add-on, WPForms, Fluent Forms, Elementor Forms).
Add a webhook to your form: URL {ADDRESS}, method POST, format JSON or form data.
Name the fields name, phone, email, city and message (or use the plugin's field mapping).
Submit the form once, then check the activity list here.
guides.note: Our own form snippet (a plain HTML form) also works on any WordPress page: use Website form instead.

guides.name: Wix Forms
steps: In Wix open Automations and make an automation: trigger Form submitted, pick your form.
Action: Send HTTP request (or Send a webhook), method POST, URL {ADDRESS}, body JSON.
Body fields: name, phone, email, city, message from the form.
Submit the form once and check the activity list here.

guides.name: Google Sheets (a new row = a new lead)
steps: The simplest way is Lead sheets here: paste your sheet's link and we read new rows every few minutes.
If you prefer pushing: in the sheet open Extensions, Apps Script, paste the script below, and add a trigger: function onRow, event source From spreadsheet, event type On change.
The sheet's first row must be the headings Name, Phone, Email, City, Message.
